issues.description: The code creates an unnecessary reference and then immediately dereferences it, which clippy detects as redundant code that should be simplified
issues.rule_name: Rust Code Must Pass Clippy Linting with Warnings Denied

issues.title: Exit command resolves after activity termination
issues.description: The exit command calls `activity.finish()` before `invoke.resolve()`. This creates a race condition where the activity lifecycle may terminate before the JavaScript callback receives the resolution response. This can lead to lost responses, potential crashes in the JavaScript layer when expecting a resolution that never arrives, and unreliable exit behavior. The resolution should occur before finishing the activity to ensure the response is sent back to the frontend before the Android activity is destroyed.

issues.title: Back navigation handled by both framework and plugin
issues.description: Setting `handleBackNavigation` to `true` in TauriActivity causes the Wry framework to handle back navigation, which conflicts with the AppPlugin's custom OnBackPressedCallback implementation. This creates competing back button handlers where both the framework's default behavior and the plugin's custom logic attempt to process back button events. This can result in double back navigation, skipped history entries, or inconsistent behavior when users press the back button. The value should remain `false` to allow the AppPlugin to be the sole handler of back button events as designed in the PR.

issues.title: Exit command not registered in build.rs permissions
issues.description: The Android exit command is implemented in AppPlugin.kt but is not registered in the Rust build.rs file under the core:app plugin commands list. Without registration in the PLUGINS constant, the exit command will not be accessible through the Tauri IPC bridge, making the exit functionality completely non-functional. All Tauri commands must be registered in build.rs to be callable from the frontend, as evidenced by the pattern used for register_listener and remove_listener commands which were properly added to the same list.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14133 - feat(core): back button event on Android, closes #8142

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds an Android back-button hook to Tauri. A new Kotlin `AppPlugin` registers an `OnBackPressedCallback`. If JS has registered a `back-button` listener, the callback triggers an event with `canGoBack`. Otherwise it falls back to `WebView.goBack()`, or to the default activity back behavior when the webview cannot go back. On the JS side it adds `onBackButtonPress()` in `@tauri-apps/api/app`, and on the Rust side it adds `register_listener`/`remove_listener` to the `core:app` ACL. `Plugin.kt` gains a `hasListener` helper, and `TauriActivity` sets `handleBackNavigation`.

The design follows the Capacitor reference and the Kotlin logic is mostly clear. However, the Rust `setup` hook does not compile on Android: it moves a non-Copy `PluginHandle` out of a shared reference. The change also bundles unrelated dependency bumps into `Cargo.lock`, leaves the `exit` command unreachable, and exposes a JS API on all platforms that has no native handler outside Android. The `handleBackNavigation` override could also double-handle back presses, and I could not verify that from this repo.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The Android build breaks because of the `*handle_ref` move in `plugin.rs`, which is a hard blocker. Beyond that, the unreachable `exit` command, the cross-platform `onBackButtonPress` export that rejects on desktop, and the unverified interaction with wry's back handling all need resolution. The Kotlin callback logic and the `hasListener` refactor are reasonable.

architecture.overview:
Today, Android back presses are handled by the WryActivity/WebView stack. Tauri's app plugin (`crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`) exposes desktop commands only, and JS calls such as `getName` go through `invoke('plugin:app|...')`. Plugin event listeners on mobile go through `Plugin.registerListener`/`trigger` in `Plugin.kt`, which stores Channels keyed by event name.

This PR adds an Android-only `AppPlugin` that is registered in the app plugin's setup hook. Its constructor installs an `OnBackPressedCallback`. The callback checks `hasListener('back-button')`: with a listener, it sends `canGoBack` to JS through the Channel. Without one, it calls `goBack()` on the WebView, or falls back to the activity's default back behavior. On the JS side, `onBackButtonPress` wraps `addPluginListener('app', 'back-button', handler)`. The ACL gains `register_listener` and `remove_listener` as default commands for `core:app`.
steps: Entry point: the user presses Android back. Before this PR the WebView handled it through the activity. Now the `AppPlugin` callback, installed in its `init` block, receives the press first.

JS side: `onBackButtonPress` in `packages/api/src/app.ts` calls `addPluginListener`, which invokes `plugin:app|register_listener` with a Channel. `build.rs` adds this command to the `core:app` ACL as default-enabled.

Android plugin registration: `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs` setup calls `register_android_plugin('app.tauri','AppPlugin')` and tries to store the handle with `manage`. This is the step that fails to compile.

Native dispatch: `AppPlugin.kt` checks `hasListener` (added to `Plugin.kt`). With a listener it calls `trigger` to send `canGoBack` to JS. Without one it navigates the WebView back or finishes the activity. `exit` is defined but not exposed through the ACL or JS.
Activity wiring: `TauriActivity.kt` (codegen template) sets `handleBackNavigation = true`, which must be coordinated with wry's own back handling so the two callbacks do not conflict.

findings.title: `*handle_ref` moves out of a shared borrow, so Android fails to compile
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`, the `setup` closure around lines 135-143 does `_app.manage(AppPlugin(*handle_ref))` where `handle_ref = &handle`. `PluginHandle` is only `Clone`, not `Copy`, so this fails with E0507 on Android. Remove the `handle_ref` binding and pass `handle` by value to `AppPlugin`. Also check whether the managed `AppPlugin` state is actually used anywhere; if it is not, drop the `manage` call and the `AppPlugin` struct at the bottom of the file, keeping the registration with `register_android_plugin`. Keep the `#[cfg(target_os = "android")]` gate.

findings.title: `onBackButtonPress` is exported on every platform but has no native handler outside Android
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/api/src/app.ts` around lines 255-275, `onBackButtonPress` calls `addPluginListener('app','back-button',...)`, which invokes `plugin:app|register_listener`. That command is only implemented by the Android `Plugin.kt` base class, so desktop and iOS calls reject. Decide on a platform contract: either guard the function so it resolves to a no-op or throws a clear error outside Android, or document it as Android-only. Check the `isAndroid`-style helper used elsewhere in `packages/api` for the pattern. Also reconsider whether `register_listener` and `remove_listener` should stay default-enabled in `crates/tauri/build.rs` (lines 167-168) for all platforms.

findings.title: `exit` command is unreachable from JS and the ACL
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt` (lines 48-53) the `exit` @Command is never exposed. `crates/tauri/build.rs` `core:app` list (around line 167) does not include it, so no ACL permission is generated and the TS API has no wrapper. Either remove `exit`, or add `("exit", false)` to the build.rs list, add a TS `exit()` wrapper in `packages/api/src/app.ts` that calls `plugin:app|exit`, and regenerate the autogenerated permissions reference following the existing pattern. Pick one and keep the Kotlin, build.rs, and TS in sync.

findings.title: Registering a listener silently disables the default WebView back behavior
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt` lines 29-44, when a `back-button` listener is registered the callback only calls `trigger` and never falls back to WebView `goBack()` or the activity default. Document this in the `onBackButtonPress` JSDoc in `packages/api/src/app.ts` (lines 255-275) so app authors know they must implement navigation themselves. Optionally add a way for JS to request the native default (for example, a command that performs goBack or finish), but only if it is added to the build.rs ACL as well.

findings.title: `handleBackNavigation` override may double-handle back presses (needs verification)
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android-codegen/TauriActivity.kt` line 15, `TauriActivity` overrides `handleBackNavigation = true`. Check wry 0.53.4's `WryActivity` to see what this property does and whether its default back handling already calls `webView.goBack()`. If so, `AppPlugin`'s `OnBackPressedCallback` in `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt` will be preempted or duplicated, and JS `back-button` listeners will be bypassed. Either remove the override, or ensure `AppPlugin` is the only owner of back handling. Add a note in the change explaining which applies.

findings.title: Unrelated dependency bumps bundled into a feature PR
findings.fixPrompt: The PR `Cargo.lock` (around the `wry` entry at line 10949) and `crates/tauri-runtime-wry/Cargo.toml` line 20 bump wry from 0.53.2 to 0.53.4. The lock also changes several `windows-sys` and `windows-targets` transitive versions unrelated to the back-button feature. Revert these unrelated dependency bumps so the PR only contains the Android back-button change, or, if the wry bump is required, document why in the PR description and changelog and confirm Windows and macOS builds still pass.

findings.title: `AppPlugin` is stored in managed state that nothing reads
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`, the `setup` closure stores the Android plugin handle in managed state (`_app.manage(AppPlugin(...))`, around line 140), and the `pub(crate) struct AppPlugin` at lines 147-148 is never read. Confirm nothing calls `state::<AppPlugin<...>>()`. If nothing does, remove the `manage` call and the struct. Also rename `_app`/`_api` to `app`/`api` since they are used on Android. Keep the `register_android_plugin` call.

findings.title: No tests cover the new back-button path or the permission defaults
findings.fixPrompt: Add test coverage for the new `onBackButtonPress` in `packages/api/src/app.ts` (lines 255-275). Follow the existing `packages/api` test pattern for mocking `invoke` and checking that `addPluginListener` calls `plugin:app|register_listener` with event `back-button` and a Channel. Also consider a check that `crates/tauri/permissions/app/autogenerated/reference.md` matches the `core:app` default list in `crates/tauri/build.rs` (around line 167). Keep the test focused on the wiring, not native behavior.

findings.title: Clean `hasListener` helper and unused-import cleanup in Plugin.kt
findings.body:
`hasListener` reuses the existing `listeners` map in a single expression. It keeps the back-button check in `AppPlugin` free of storage details. The imports removed from `Plugin.kt` (`Bundle`, `JSONException`) are not referenced in the file, so the cleanup is safe.

::diff{file="crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/plugin/Plugin.kt" lines="146-152"}

findings.title: Back-button fallback mirrors the webview-first default
findings.body:
With no listener, the callback goes back in the WebView history first, and only then falls back to the activity's default back action. That matches the Capacitor reference the author cites. The `webView!!` access is only reached after a `canGoBack() == true` check, so it cannot throw. Disabling the callback around `onBackPressed()` avoids re-entering the callback.

::code{file="crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt" lines="29-37"}
